ash: Heads-up — seeing a surge of GPU attach failures in us-west2, ~18% of attaches timing out and pods stuck in ContainerCreating.
ravi: Any recent deploys or janitor changes? Could be noisy-neighbor io.
ash: No deploys in the last hour. Node logs show NVMe io-queue backlog, here's a tail of the kernel log:
ash: ```\n[1728420001.123] nvme0: I/O queue full, submit timeout 2000ms
[1728420002.456] nvme0: long job: rmw write 512k blk 0x1f2a
[1728420003.789] blk_update_request: I/O error, dev nvme0n1, sector 123456
```
maya: ugh. Janitor scrub tasks started a heavy pass on ephemeral pool earlier — we suspected backlog but thought rate-limit would hold.
leo: Can we throttle the scrubber or pause it on the affected host pool? Also consider raising ioquota for gpu-pod class temporarily.
ash: Trying to correlate nodes: grabbing affected nodes list now — looks like 12 nodes across three racks.
ops-bot: Alert: gpu-attach-error-rate > 10% in us-west2 (last 5m). Auto-scaling for warm-pool disabled.
ravi: Quick mitigation: pause janitor on the hot ephemeral pools and drain scrub queue on those nodes. Command:
ravi: ```bash
./janitorctl pause --pool ephemeral-usw2-hot --reason "hot-io-backpressure" --duration 10m
for n in $(./fleetctl list-nodes --label ephemeral-usw2-hot); do ssh $n 'systemctl restart ioquota-agent'; done
```
ash: Running pause now on pools eu-west and usw2-hot (only on affected racks). Will restart ioquota-agent on the first 6 nodes.
maya: Also add a quick routing fallback so new attaches prefer warm-pool for next 15m: set routing policy -> prefer=warm-pool, ttl=15m.
leo: I'll bump ioquota from 50MB/s -> 120MB/s for the gpu workload class until the scrub completes. Monitoring disk throughput.
ash: Patch applied. Attaches in the last 30s dropped to 4% and queued attach backlog is decreasing.
ravi: Nice. Keep an eye on wear metrics — we don't want to hide a failing drive with throttles.
ash: Agreed — scheduling a follow-up inspection of SMART counters and scrub history for those nodes.
ops-bot: Note: janitorctl pause executed by ravi at 1728420032. Reaction :white_check_mark:.
maya: Plan for next steps: 1) run deeper SMART checks on the 12 nodes; 2) tune scrub cadence to avoid overlapping with heavy GPU batch windows; 3) consider transient warm-pool burst capacity for peak hours.
leo: I'll open an infra ticket with cost estimate for warm-pool burst (expected ~+3% monthly) and link the scrub cadence proposal.
ash: For the immediate runbook, leaving pause for 10m then gradually re-enable scrub at 30% rate and watch attach rate for 15m before full resume.
ravi: If attach errors bounce back >10% after resume, we'll roll to warm-pool fallback for the next 2 hours and continue investigation.
ash: Thanks all — monitoring. Will post updates if anything flares up. :eyes:
leo: :thumbsup:
ops-bot: Incident note created: INC-172842 (ephemeral io backlog affecting gpu attaches)
